alex: Quick sync — I want to propose a 'skein' refactor: unravel the enrichment monolith into three narrow services (ingest, enrich-core, policy-fence). Aim is incremental cutovers with a thin facade, no big-bang.
maria: +1. Facade must be tiny and idempotent. How do we surface telemetry while keeping it out of the hotpath? event bridge vs push metrics tradeoff.
josh: Sequence guarantees are the big one. If we split, KV cache ownership becomes sticky. Proposal: sticky routing by session-id -> state shard (not instance). That lets us relocate shards without breaking seq semantics.
alex: Agree on sticky shards. Also want to extract auth/policy checks into a 'policy fence' so we can roll out stricter rules per-tenant without touching enrich-core.
kevin: Heads-up: extra RPC hop will likely add ~3-5ms p50. Can we batch auth checks or keep a cached allowlist at the edge to reduce chattiness?
maria: We can do both: batch allow checks at the facade and maintain a local LRU cache with short TTL (30s). If cache misses, fallback to policy-fence. Need per-tenant feature flags for staged rollouts too.
josh: Operational plan: canary by tenant + route path. Router needs to support per-tenant weights. Do we have that capability today? @kevin any infra constraints?
kevin: Router can do weighted routing per path, but adding tenant dimension will need a small config surface change. Also for private deploys we'll need to ensure the router respects VPC/CORS rules. We'll add two alarms: auth_fail_rate and policy_p99_latency.
sre-bot: deploy 1737777788: canary-15% applied to staging, all checks green (0 errors) for 90s.
alex: Next steps: - PR for facade shim by EOW (alex) - policy-fence prototype (maria) - router weight toggle (kevin) - perf microbenchmark on staging (josh). I'll draft an RFC summary and attach a rollout checklist.
maria: Ack. I'll also prototype TTL cache interface: `class PolicyCache { get(key): Promise<boolean> }` and a small harness to simulate churn.
josh: For KV shard rehashing: keep ownership coarse (tenant -> shard); rehash plan: add new shard -> tombstone old mapping -> migrate gracefully within window. Sketch: `shard = hash(tenant_id) % N` with reassign epoch markers.
alex: Sounds good. We should also document failure modes (policy fence down => degrade to lax allowlist with metric tagging). I'll put that in the RFC and create a small incident playbook.
maria: One more: add e2e tests that assert no request duplication and session ordering across cutover.
kevin: I'll make router change low-risk: feature flag off by default, toggleable per-tenant. Will add the two alarms and an SLO for policy latency.
alex: Great. Sync next Tues 10am to validate prototype results. :calendar:
